To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a large hexanucletide repeat expansion in the intron of the C9ORF7 gene on chromosome 9p, which is the genetic cause of chromosome 9p-linked ALS FTD in the Finnish population and in a third of familial ALS in outbred European populations.
We have discovered that a repeat expansion in the intron of the C9ORF7 gene is the cause of chromosome 9p-linked familial ALS and FTD.
we have found a large hexanuclear repeat expansion in the intron of C-9 ORF 72 that causes ALS-FTD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular and cellular basis of neurodegenerative disease and in particular the mechanisms underlying the selective vulnerability of specific neuronal populations in these diseases.
the identification of genetic factors that contribute to the risk of developing ALS, a devastating and currently incurable disease.
the genetic and biochemical basis of motor neuron disease and dementia, which together constitute the common neurodegeneratative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hexanucleotide expansion in C9ORFR72 is the most common cause of ALS in Europe and North America.
the C9ORF gene is the cause of chromosome 9p linked ALS FTD.
C9ORF7 is the gene underlying chromosome 9p linked ALS FTD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a repeat expansion in C9ORf72 as the cause of chromosome 9p linked familial ALS and FTD.
we have discovered a new disease causing mutation in the C9ORF gene.
we have identified the first repeat expansion in a human disease gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we now have a simple explanation of the genetics of ALS and FTD in the Finnish population.
the C9ORF gene contains the largest hexanucleotide repeat expansion known in humans.
the hexanucleotide repeat expansion in C9ORFR72 causes ALS and FTD in a large proportion of ALS cases in the Finnish population and in a significant proportion of ALS cases of European descent.
